rv.q: If you've been craving a break from the frights of real life, this campy, vampy romp is a scream.
Unfortunately, in this case, the second half of the evening drags a bit.
Too bad for them, because this “Comedy of Terrors” is a scream.
This Dracula should be here for a long visit to our shores.
No amount of description can convey the delights of this ingenious rejiggering.
It is an accomplished 90-minute diversion inciting abundant audience laughter.

The show makes it difficult to begrudge pointing out the occasional imprecise, maybe, I’ll say it, potentially transphobic ‘man in a dress’ nature to some of the jokes because, after all, it advertises itself as a gender-bending reenvisioning of the text.
Greenberg, who also directs, and Rosen are blessed with an extremely versatile cast: With the exception of Daly, all the actors play two or more parts.
However, you may die laughing during its 90-minute run.
Run to see this show and treat yourself this Halloween season, Kids.
Utilizing elements of romantic comedy, farce, puppetry and high camp, playwrights Gordon Greenberg and Steve Rosen serve up a confection that is keenly unwrapped by an ensemble cast of five.
The show is a fun, pleasant jaunt with wordplay and some popular cultural references.

Before it became known as a vehicle for strippers and baggy pants comics, burlesque meant parodies of well-known plays and musical theatre. And that latter meaning perfectly applies to Dracula: A Comedy of Terrors, Gordon Greenberg and Steve Rosen’s comic bite out of Bram Stoker’s 1897 vampire novel, Dracula.
